extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international/diplomatic/military news
extracted.subtask_description: Writing news reports about sudden international/diplomatic/military crises, combining official statements, eyewitness accounts, political context, and analysis of motives and resources. Emphasizes attribution, verification, and background to explain developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute extraordinary claims to official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: An official announcement said that the Bucharest negotiations were 'continuing their normal course and that all reports "going beyond this fact are to be regarded as an attempt to create a condition of tension.' The announcement added that 'the contention that Germany presented an ultimatum to Rumania is, of course, pure invention, lacking every basis in fact.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting claims that could inflame opinion (ultimatums, provocations), attribute them to named official statements and present official denials verbatim where available; mark disputed claims as such rather than asserting them as facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish verified facts from reports, rumors, or 'it was understood' accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases used in the text include 'it was understood, moreover, that...', 'reports said', 'it was said', and 'official sources had denied any extraordinary ...' to separate confirmed facts from circulating accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualifiers (reported, it was understood, official sources deny) to indicate level of verification; avoid presenting conjecture as confirmed fact and clearly label sourcing for less-certain material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide military movement specifics (units, locations, logistics)
rubrics_metrics.description: The article gives concrete detail: 'An estimated 200,000 Hungarian troops were in Eastern Ruthenia... troops dug deep ditches... columns of soldiers hauling heavy artillery through the snow... workmen were following the occupation army.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numbers, unit types, geographic markers, and logistical details (roads blocked, barbed wire, artillery movement) to convey the scale and character of military actions; attribute such details to reports or observers when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on economic motives and resource importance
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece explains why Rumania mattered: 'Rumania, rich in oil, and wheat... in 1937 Rumania was the world's sixth largest producer of oil... an important byproduct of her oil wells is natural gas.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background on economic resources, trade proposals, and strategic materials that may motivate diplomatic or military actions; include production figures and trade relationship details where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document diplomatic negotiations and proposed treaties with attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports that 'the trade negotiations... were being conducted... Foreign Minister Grigore Gafencu insisted, however, that Germany had presented nothing.' Also: 'Dr. Wohlthat... continues negotiations for the carrying out of the economic agreement signed between Germany and Rumania as far back as November 1938.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe ongoing negotiations, treaty proposals, and the positions of named diplomats and delegations; note when proposals are denied or characterized as pressure rather than formal terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include humanitarian impact: refugee and arrest counts with sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: 'The World Jewish Congress published "an appeal..." It declared that 250,000 more Jews "find themselves under the necessity..."' and counts like '87,000 in Moravia... 69,000 in Carpatho-Ukraine... 71 percent German-speaking.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on refugees, arrests, or persecution, supply numbers and identify the reporting organization (League, Congress, governments); present these figures as sourced and contextualize humanitarian consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report local social atmosphere and visible signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Local observations include 'No Jews Wanted signs appeared in coffee houses... signs appeared in stores designating the owners as German, Czech or Jewish' and 'Prague residents continued their silent demonstrations... stood without tears.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include on-the-ground descriptions of public mood, demonstrations, signage, and everyday social impacts to humanize the story and illustrate changes in civic life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain ideological and strategic motives (e.g., 'all Germans', 'lebensraum')
rubrics_metrics.description: The article states two cardinal principles: 'all Germans, under the protection of Hitler...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should explain the ideological doctrines or strategic aims behind actors' actions (quoting doctrine terms like "bring home into the Reich" and "lebensraum") so readers understand motivations driving territorial moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document propaganda and covert operations when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece asserts the annexation 'was built on a carefully planned and executed propaganda campaign by Nazi experts... undercovers agents and operatives... their purpose to bring Czechoslovak political policies more in harmony with the Reich.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting on influence operations or propaganda, name identified organizers and summarize methods (undercover agents, published bans, distribution of funds) and provide examples of their effects on institutions and public opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report domestic political responses and emergency measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: 'Premier Edouard Daladier, armed with unprecedented dictatorial powers... called to the colors 125,000 special fortress troops... the Senate had completed Parliamentary action turning France into a virtual dictatorship until November 30.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail government reactions: decrees, mobilization orders, checks on executive power, and legislative changes; include dates, scope, and stated justifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use historical and geographic context to situate events
rubrics_metrics.description: The article situates regions and past events: references to 'since the Munich conference', Austro-Sudeten annexations, Memel, Danzig, the Polish Corridor, and the strategic location bordering the Soviet Ukrainian Ukraine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide relevant historical precedents, territorial descriptions, and geographic connections to help readers understand continuity and regional implications of current events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance multiple international reactions and forecasts
rubrics_metrics.description: The text reports reactions from Britain, France, Italy, Soviet circles, Swiss statements, League of Nations appeals, and speculation ('What is the next thing up Hitler's sleeve?').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include statements and actions from a range of international actors, record diplomatic exchanges or conferences under consideration, and present expert or official speculation as such to reflect the international dimension.
